lede: Gold jumped about 2% back above $3,600 in Asian trade as falling Treasury yields and Friday's equity rout led traders to trim, but not abandon, bets on a December Fed hike. Bitcoin is holding near $60,000 after a seventh straight weekly loss, its longest losing run since the 2022 Terra collapse.
snapshot_time: Gold ~06:40 TRT, EURUSD ~07:00 TRT Mon · US500 & Brent = Fri 20 Nov close

focus.text: Rebounding from a double bottom near $3,503 to ~$3,604, now above its 3,571 pivot as yields slip. US flash PMIs (17:45 TRT) are today's test; Wednesday's PCE looms.
Edging up to ~1.0984, just above the 1.0975 pivot but still pinned under 1.10 near 19-month lows. Euro-area flash PMIs at 12:00 TRT, US PMIs at 17:45.

technicals.indicators: Daily RSI(14) ≈ 21, deeply oversold · far below 50/200-day MAs · hourly RSI back above 50
technicals.note: A double bottom around $3,500–3,520 is driving a rebound inside a steep downtrend that has produced lower highs since the early-November peak near $4,150.
The pair is compressing in a tight 1.0953–1.1035 band right at its 2026 low, with the 1.10 handle acting as a ceiling.

technicals.indicators: Seven straight weekly losses · Fear & Greed 11 (extreme fear) · funding briefly negative
technicals.note: Saturday's flush to about $55,100 was bought back toward $61,000, but price remains inside a falling weekly structure that has cut roughly 30% since early October.

technicals.indicators: Lowest levels since July · weekly loss ~18% to Saturday
technicals.note: ETH has reclaimed $1,700 after a weekend dip near $1,541, leaving the $1,541–1,550 zone as the swing low to watch.

news.text: US Treasury Secretary Bessent cautioned that further Fed tightening could endanger growth; markets still price a 25bp December hike as near-certain, though slightly less so.
S&P 500 is in correction after an 8.6% weekly drop; Friday's 3.7% slide was led by Nvidia (−13.8%) on reports of an SEC accounting probe.
Treasuries rallied into the weekend: the 2-year yield fell about 11bp to 4.64% and the 10-year eased to roughly 4.91%, taking some heat off the dollar.
Iran tensions stay high: Trump signalled renewed military action after New Year without a deal, while Iran claimed strikes on US radars in Bahrain.
Brent sits near $92 after a third weekly decline; the UAE is moving crude through Hormuz under US military escort, and OPEC+ meets on Sunday.
Bitcoin logged a seventh consecutive weekly loss, closing the week near $60,100 after briefly sliding to roughly $55,100 on Saturday.
US spot bitcoin ETFs have bled about $3.5bn so far in November, including a record single-day $541m outflow from BlackRock's IBIT.
Chainflip lost around $12m in an attack on its vaults and offered the attacker a $1.2m bounty; FLIP fell as much as 37%.
Solana hovered near $70 as SOL ETFs snapped a six-week outflow streak and the network marked its mainnet 1.0 upgrade.
Hong Kong published draft licensing rules for virtual-asset dealers and custodians; the UK plans to bar exchanges from market-making on their own venues.
Monad (MON) unlocks about 32% of circulating supply, worth roughly $219m, on Tuesday — the week's largest scheduled token release.

week_ahead.intro: A holiday-shortened US week revolves around Wednesday's October PCE inflation, the last major price gauge before the Fed's 9 December meeting, where a 25bp hike is almost fully priced. Markets arrive bruised after the S&P 500's worst week in 19 months, gold's ~9% slide and bitcoin's seventh weekly loss.

themes.text: PCE and the Beige Book decide whether December hike pricing firms or fades; Fed speakers go quiet from Saturday.
After an AI-led stock correction and VIX spike, the question is whether Monday's bounce in gold and yields-driven relief can hold.
Monday's flash PMIs for the euro area, UK and US give the first read on November activity.
Thanksgiving (Thu) and a US half-day (Fri) thin out trading, which can exaggerate moves in FX, gold and crypto.
Iran–US friction and attacks on shipping keep a risk premium in oil ahead of Sunday's OPEC+ meeting.
